analysis.title: Potential for a "blue wave" has consequences for US policy extending into 2028 (Coffee Break, 30 October 2026)
key_insights: Polling has shifted against Republicans ahead of the 3 November midterms. YouGov shows Democrats ahead by 6 points nationally, versus 1 point at the start of Trump's second term.
Trump's approval in the Cook Political Report poll of polls is 37% approve and 61% disapprove, versus 47% approve and 49% disapprove at the start of his term.

Cook moved 19 more House races toward Democrats and rates 218 of 435 seats as favoured outright for them, enough for a majority. With 17 toss-ups, it projects a Democratic House of 227 to 237 seats. Cook says a Republican path to a House majority 'has all but evaporated'.
Republicans hold the House narrowly with 219 seats plus one independent who caucuses with them.

Senate control is less certain. Republicans hold 53-47, Democrats need to flip 4 of the 33 seats up, and the map favours Republicans. Up to 10 seats are toss-ups, and Democrats lead polls in 8 of them (RealClearPolitics, within the margin of error).

Trump won several competitive Senate states by more than 10 points in 2024 (Iowa, Nebraska, Kansas, Ohio, South Carolina, Texas, Alaska), which shows how much harder the map has become for Republicans.
Cook projects Democratic Senate gains of 2 to 6 seats, so a majority is a distinct possibility but not assured.

Prediction markets and leading pollsters put the odds of a Democratic House at about 90% and a Democratic Senate at about 60%. UniCredit flags considerable uncertainty, partly because of the Republican funding advantage.

Even a 'blue wave' would not let Democrats override a veto or the filibuster. They would gain oversight powers, and are already planning initiatives and investigations that would curtail the president's ability to set the policy agenda.
At least 49 local ballot initiatives in 13 states involve data centres, AI and electricity demand. They will test whether these become a partisan issue.

Trump's reaction to the result could move markets. A major defeat could prompt him to lash out internationally or issue executive orders, or push his own party to press for a change of direction. A minor loss could be read as outperformance, as with Biden's 9-seat House loss and 1-seat Senate gain in 2022.
BoJ held at 1.25% with one dissenter favouring an immediate hike. Core CPI median forecasts were raised only for 2027, to 2.6% yoy from 2.4%.
Forwards price only a 60% chance of the 25bp BoJ hike UniCredit expects on 18 December.

AI-related equity weakness spread from the US to Asia overnight, with KOSPI falling the most. The 10Y UST yield fell to 4.93%, approaching the 4.80% level of early September before the bond sell-off, and transatlantic spreads tightened.
EUR-USD is back near 1.12 after a YTD low of 1.1106 the day before. Political tensions still limit a sustained euro recovery.

macro_indicators.interpretation: BoJ held, with one dissenter favouring an immediate hike.
The only year with a raised projection. The 2026 forecast is unchanged at 2.5% and the 2028 forecast at 2.0%.

macro_indicators.reading: 25bp hike expected by UniCredit; forwards price 60% likelihood
macro_indicators.interpretation: Market pricing is below UniCredit's expectation of a hike.
Yields fell on AI-driven equity weakness and are nearing the 4.80% level of early September, before the bond sell-off.
The USD weakened. The prior day's YTD low gives the pair a cushion to the downside.

risk_factors: Midterm outcome uncertainty, especially for the Senate, where the map favours Republicans and they have a funding advantage.
Trump's reaction to a midterm defeat, through international actions or executive orders, could move markets.
Renewed AI-related concerns are dragging on equities worldwide.
Upside inflation risks keep the BoJ focused on CPI, and forwards price only a 60% chance of the December hike.
geopolitical: US midterm elections on 3 November 2026, with control of the House and Senate at stake.
Possible reaction by Trump to a midterm defeat, either internationally or through executive orders.
Political tensions limiting a sustained recovery of the euro.

tension_points.bull_case: Democrats have a viable path to a Senate majority. They lead polls in 8 of up to 10 toss-up seats, and Cook projects gains of 2 to 6 seats. Prediction markets and pollsters put the odds near 60%.
tension_points.bear_case: Democrats need 4 flips on an unfavourable map, many of the toss-up leads are within the polling margin of error, and Republicans have a significant funding advantage.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Results on 3 November in the toss-up Senate states, where Democrats need to flip 4 seats from the 53-47 Republican majority.

tension_points.bull_case: A minor Republican defeat could be read as outperformance, as with Biden in 2022, and affirm Trump's policies and his place at the centre of the party.
tension_points.bear_case: A major defeat could lead Trump to lash out internationally or through executive orders, or put him under pressure from his own party to change direction, which could roil markets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The size of the Republican losses in the House and Senate on 3 November.

theme_stances.key_argument: Polling has deteriorated for Republicans, a Democratic House looks increasingly likely, and the Senate is a viable but uncertain path.
theme_stances.evidence: Democrats have a viable path to gain a majority in the Senate

theme_stances.key_argument: The BoJ remains focused on upside inflation risks, and UniCredit expects a 25bp hike on 18 December although forwards price only 60%.
theme_stances.evidence: A 25bp rate hike is expected at the meeting on 18 December
